The thinking behind it

Less “responsible for.”
More “here’s what
I made happen.”

Your resume is a selection of evidence. Start with the person reading it, and give them a reason to keep going.

A working approach, inspired by Zach’s resumes.

Make a personal site ↗

From the archive

Different opportunity.
Different emphasis.

The structure should serve the story. These examples show how the emphasis changes across Zach’s supplied applications.

2026 / Career & entrepreneurship+

A compact header, supporting education and skills, and a primary experience column. The takeaway: make the big picture readable before adding detail.

2024 / Graduate school+

The Booth and Kellogg versions lead with a tailored summary and leadership experience. Education, community work, and contribution help explain why the next step matters.

Notion / Enterprise sales+

Separate “Results” blocks distinguish activity from outcomes. Try the same exercise: describe what you did, then write the evidence that it worked.
